scope: P10 durable music queues and explicit paused restoration after backend restart.
implemented: Music queues are stored per voice channel with their stable queue item IDs, repeat mode and monotonic revision.
Queue changes, playback completion, shuffle, reorder, repeat changes and temporary bot shutdown persist a current snapshot.
A backend restart loads saved sessions into an inactive paused state without connecting to LiveKit or beginning playback.
An authorized explicit restore endpoint reconnects the publisher; the client exposes this action only for a saved paused queue.
An unexpected LiveKit publisher disconnect snapshots the interrupted track and pending queue into the same paused recovery state instead of silently discarding them or auto-playing.
Stopping playback intentionally removes the durable session while a graceful server shutdown preserves it.
Deleting the owning channel or server removes the session through foreign-key cascades.
remaining: Two real clients must verify audible restoration, concurrent queue mutations and reconnect behavior against LiveKit.
A packaged Windows build must verify that restart restoration remains paused and never auto-joins a voice channel.
release: Source and automated fixtures only; no commit, push, merge, deployment or Windows update was performed.
